The accused persons (petitioners herein) after compromising the matter with complainant/respondent No. 3 and respondent No. 4, have come up before this Court under Section 482 Cr.P.C., by invoking inherent powers of this Court, seeking quashing of FIR No. 90 of 2019,
dated 11.04.2019, under Sections 498-A, 504, 506 and 34 of the Indian Penal Code (for short "IPC"),
registered at Police Station Baddi, District Solan, H.P..

6. I have heard learned counsel for the petitioners, learned Additional Advocate General for respondents No.1 & 2/State as well as the learned counsel for complainant/respondent No. 3 and respondent No. 4 and .
also gone through the material available on record.

7. In Gian Singh Vs. State of Punjab and others, reported in (2012) 10 SCC 303, explaining that High Court has inherent power under Section 482 of the Code of of Criminal Procedure with no statutory limitation, including Section 320 Cr.PC, the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that rt these powers are to be exercised to secure the ends of justice or to prevent abuse of process of any Court and these powers can be exercised to quash criminal proceedings or complaint or FIR in appropriate cases where offender and victim have settled their dispute and for that purpose no definite category of offence can be prescribed.

entities.text: Gian Singh Vs. State of Punjab and others, reported in (2012) 10 SCC 303
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, it is also observed that Courts must have due regard to nature and gravity of the crime and criminal proceedings in heinous and serious offences or offences like murder, rape and dacoity etc. should not be quashed despite victim or victim's family have settled the dispute with offender.

Jurisdiction vested in High Court under Section 482 Cr.PC is held to be exercisable for quashing criminal proceedings in cases having overwhelming and predominately civil flavour particularly offences arising from commercial, financial, .
mercantile, civil partnership, or such like transactions, or even offences arising out of matrimony relating to dowry etc., family disputes or other such disputes where wrong is basically private or personal nature where parties mutually of resolve their dispute amicably.

It was also held that no category or cases for this purpose could be prescribed and rt each case has to be dealt with on its own merit but it is also clarified that this power does not extend to crimes against society.

8. Further, the Apex Court in Parbatbhai Aahir alias Parbhathbhai Bhimsinghbhai Karmur and others vs. State of Gujarat and another, (2017) 9 SCC 641, summarizing the broad principles regarding inherent powers of the High Court under Section 482 Cr.PC. has recognized that these powers are not inhibited by provisions of Section 320 Cr.PC.
9.

sentences.text: , the Hon'ble Supreme Court emphasized and advised that in the matter of compromise in criminal proceedings, keeping in view the nature of the case, to save the time of the Court for utilizing to decide more effective and meaningful litigation, a common sense approach, based on ground of realities and bereft of the technicalities of law, should be applied.

11. In the instant case, since the matter has been amicably settled between the parties, therefore,
keeping in view the nature of the offence, I am of the considered view that no fruitful purpose will be served to continue the proceedings against petitioners/accused persons, as continuation of the proceedings will be an exercise in futility.
Moreover, respondent No. 4 is now living happily with her .
husband, i.e., petitioner No. 1 under one roof, therefore, continuation of the proceedings would cause immense harm to her, as the same may adversely affect her marital life.
of Therefore, the justice in the case demands that the dispute between the parties is put to an end and peace is restored in rt order to maintain harmonious relations/atmosphere between them.

12. Hence, considering the facts and the circumstances of the case in entirety, I am of the opinion that the present petition deserves to be allowed for securing the ends of justice and, therefore, the same is allowed.

Accordingly, FIR No. 90 of 2019, dated 11.04.2019, under Sections 498-A, 504, 506 and 34 IPC,
registered against the petitioners/accused, at Police Station Baddi, District Solan, H.P., and the consequent proceedings, arising out of the said FIR, pending before the learned Judicial Magistrate First Class, Nalagarh, District Solan, H.P., are ordered to be quashed and set-aside.
